topic: Akainu's real target at Marineford was Ace and Luffy's lineage, not Whitebeard
title: Why Akainu Chased Ace Instead Of Whitebeard
description:
At Marineford, Akainu barely tries to finish Whitebeard, the strongest pirate alive. He spends the entire war aiming at one lineage instead: Gol D. Roger's. Here's the chapter-by-chapter case that Akainu's Absolute Justice was never about raw power at all.

From Sengoku's reveal in chapter 550 to the moment Akainu aims past Ace at Luffy in chapter 573, every choice the Fleet Admiral makes points the same direction. Whitebeard was contained. Ace and Luffy were hunted.
comment: Was Akainu ever actually trying to kill Whitebeard, or was the Emperor just in his way the whole time?

lines.text: Akainu didn't spend Marineford hunting Whitebeard. He spent it hunting one lineage, and Whitebeard wasn't in it.

shot.fallback: red haired marine admiral facing a giant old pirate

lines.text: Ace was Gol D. Roger's son, and that is the only reason Akainu wanted him gone before the war even began.

shot.fallback: young fire pirate standing before a crowd

lines.text: So why does the most feared Admiral in the Marines barely land a real hit on the strongest man alive?

shot.fallback: stern admiral facing an old emperor

lines.text: Whitebeard carried the biggest bounty on that entire battlefield, which makes what happens next even stranger...

shot.fallback: towering old pirate with a giant naginata

lines.text: The actual target order was written for one specific name, and it was never the man holding a naginata...

shot.fallback: admiral staring past a battlefield

lines.text: Chapter 550 is where this war actually starts, and it has nothing to do with Whitebeard's name.

shot.fallback: marine fleet admiral addressing a crowd

lines.text: Sengoku drags Ace onto that platform and makes him answer one question in front of the entire world.

shot.fallback: fleet admiral questioning a young pirate

lines.text: Ace says Whitebeard is his father. Sengoku tells everyone listening that he's wrong.

shot.fallback: young pirate answering calmly on a platform

lines.text: Portgas D. Rouge carried Ace for twenty months, far past any natural birth, just to keep him alive.

shot.fallback: mother protecting an unborn child

lines.text: She passed away doing it, one year and three months after Gol D. Roger was gone.

shot.fallback: grieving mother in a quiet village

lines.text: Sengoku says the name out loud, over a Den Den Mushi broadcast the entire world can hear.

shot.fallback: fleet admiral speaking into a transponder snail

lines.text: Ace isn't just Whitebeard's son by choice anymore. He's the Pirate King's son by lineage.

shot.fallback: young pirate realizing his own name

lines.text: Ace spent his whole life believing nobody wanted the son of a 'devil' to even exist in the first place.

shot.fallback: young boy standing alone with doubt

lines.text: Whitebeard never saw it that way. He told Ace that lineage wasn't a curse he had to carry alone.

shot.fallback: old emperor reassuring a young pirate

lines.text: Garp himself had promised Roger he would watch over Ace, because an unborn child carries no sin for being born.

shot.fallback: marine hero holding a sleeping infant

lines.text: That single sentence from Sengoku is the entire reason this war exists in the first place.

shot.fallback: battlefield assembling around a platform

lines.text: Chinjao, from the old generation, later admits in chapter 719 that Ace showed more promise than anyone in the new one.

shot.fallback: old warrior acknowledging a young rival

lines.text: He even calls Ace's loss good for the Marines, which tells you how rare that kind of lineage really is.

shot.fallback: aging warrior speaking with grim approval

lines.text: Chapter 551 explains why the World Government was willing to start that war over one pirate at all.

shot.fallback: fleet admiral briefing marine officers

lines.text: Sengoku tells his own Marines that Ace's rise in power is exactly what exposed his lineage.

shot.fallback: admiral warning marine officers

lines.text: Left alone, Sengoku says, Ace could realistically become the next Pirate King himself.

shot.fallback: young pirate commander standing confident

lines.text: That's not one old man's paranoia. That's the official justification written for Marineford.

shot.fallback: marine headquarters preparing for war

lines.text: Whitebeard isn't the one on trial here. A lineage is, and the verdict was written before the war started...

shot.fallback: old emperor standing amid marine ships

lines.text: Akainu's entire worldview runs on one idea: some people are criminals the moment they're born.

shot.fallback: admiral speaking with cold conviction

lines.text: He already treats Luffy as a threat purely for being Dragon's son, long before Luffy does anything at Marineford.

shot.fallback: admiral watching a young pirate with suspicion

lines.text: So a boy who is literally Gol D. Roger's lineage was never going to be an afterthought in this plan.

shot.fallback: young pirate marked as a threat

lines.text: He was the target before the first Marine ship even reached Marineford Bay.

shot.fallback: fleet of warships approaching a fortress

lines.text: Chapter 573 has Akainu saying it outright: Ace and Luffy both deserve a sentence for their parentage alone.

shot.fallback: admiral pointing with burning conviction

lines.text: Not for anything they did. For what their lineage was carrying.

shot.fallback: admiral delivering a harsh verdict

lines.text: Whitebeard, by comparison, is just the strongest pirate alive. No forbidden lineage, no secret lineage to erase.

shot.fallback: old emperor standing without a hidden secret

lines.text: Nico Robin lived almost the same sentence years earlier: her existence alone was treated as a crime by this government.

shot.fallback: young archaeologist marked by a government

lines.text: The World Government doesn't wait for a D. to act. It sentences the name the moment the name is confirmed.

shot.fallback: shadowy tribunal marking a name

lines.text: That's the machine Akainu serves, and he serves it without a flicker of doubt.

shot.fallback: admiral standing rigid and loyal

lines.text: In Akainu's math, raw strength is a problem you contain. Lineage is a problem you erase.

shot.fallback: admiral weighing two different threats

lines.text: Twenty-two years earlier, Akainu was already there for the Ohara Buster Call, the government's first attempt at erasing a forbidden kind of knowledge.

shot.fallback: hooded marine officer watching a burning library

lines.text: Robin survived that purge only by becoming the exact kind of fugitive this government has hunted ever since.

shot.fallback: young archaeologist fleeing a burning island

lines.text: By the time Ace stands on that platform, Akainu has already spent decades enforcing the same idea: existence itself can be the charge.

shot.fallback: admiral carrying decades of conviction

lines.text: That one distinction decides almost everything that happens for the rest of this war...

shot.fallback: battlefield shifting into chaos

lines.text: Here's the detail most power-scaling videos skip completely.

shot.fallback: battlefield detail easy to miss

lines.text: When Akainu first steps up against Whitebeard, he isn't actually trying to kill him.

shot.fallback: admiral confronting an old emperor

lines.text: Chapter 567 shows him stopping Whitebeard's naginata swing for one specific reason: it's about to level the island.

shot.fallback: admiral blocking a massive weapon

lines.text: Whitebeard tells him to try and protect the island instead, and their powers finally collide.

shot.fallback: magma and quake powers clashing

lines.text: Listen to what Akainu is actually angry about here. It's the damage, not Whitebeard surviving the hit.

shot.fallback: admiral furious at destruction

lines.text: That's a man managing a disaster, not a man hunting a target.

shot.fallback: admiral restraining a larger threat

lines.text: Vice Admiral Momonga told Hancock that all three Admirals would lead against the Whitebeard Pirates once Ace's sentence was announced.

shot.fallback: vice admiral informing a warlord

lines.text: Notice that order: lead against the Pirates, to secure one sentence. Not hunt down an Emperor.

shot.fallback: marine officers reading an operation order

lines.text: Kizaru and Aokiji spend most of that early fight on crowd control, freezing waves and vaporizing icebergs, not chasing Whitebeard.

shot.fallback: two admirals managing a battlefield

lines.text: All three Admirals only escalate once Whitebeard's own quakes threaten to sink the entire sentence platform.

shot.fallback: three admirals bracing for a shockwave

lines.text: That's three of the strongest men alive, all reacting to Whitebeard, and none of them opening the fight against him.

shot.fallback: trio of admirals standing defensive

lines.text: Compare that to how Akainu talks about Ace and Luffy in those exact same chapters.

shot.fallback: admiral speaking of two young pirates

lines.text: With them, it's always extermination language. With Whitebeard, it's always containment language.

shot.fallback: admiral drawing a clear line

lines.text: And Whitebeard was never going to make any of this easy, lineage or not.

shot.fallback: old emperor standing immovable

lines.text: His own health is collapsing in real time, because he refuses medication just to stay in the fight.

shot.fallback: aging emperor straining to stand

lines.text: Chapter 569 shows him trying to use Supreme King Haki to shield Ace from the executioners.

shot.fallback: old emperor channeling dark power

lines.text: He fails. Not because Akainu stops him, but because a sudden illness attack does it first.

shot.fallback: emperor collapsing from sickness

lines.text: Even Kaido ranked Whitebeard alongside Roger and Oden, as one of the only men who could stand with them.

shot.fallback: dragon warlord acknowledging legends

lines.text: An old man's failing body was doing more damage to that reputation than any Admiral ever managed.

shot.fallback: weakened emperor amid a storm

lines.text: Garp, from that same wartime generation as Whitebeard, still walks away from this war without his own lineage ever getting sentenced.

shot.fallback: veteran marine standing apart from judgment

lines.text: Strength alone clearly isn't what earns that sentence. Garp has plenty of it, and nobody ever calls his existence the crime.

shot.fallback: veteran marine standing unthreatened

lines.text: Which raises the actual question here: why spend resources on someone time is already working against for you?

shot.fallback: admiral calculating a battlefield choice

lines.text: If Akainu wanted Whitebeard gone fast, chapter 561 shows exactly how he'd have done it.

shot.fallback: admiral speaking quietly to a pirate captain

lines.text: He doesn't challenge Whitebeard directly. He goes after a captain already carrying a grudge against Roger.

shot.fallback: admiral approaching a bitter pirate captain

lines.text: That captain is Squard, who lost his entire crew to Roger years earlier.

shot.fallback: grieving pirate captain alone at sea

lines.text: Whitebeard took Squard in afterward and raised him like one of his own sons.

shot.fallback: old emperor welcoming a broken pirate

lines.text: Akainu feigns sympathy and tells Squard that Whitebeard plans to abandon the allied crews just to save Ace.

shot.fallback: admiral whispering a manipulative lie

lines.text: It's a lie built specifically to turn one lineage grudge into a blade aimed at Whitebeard's own back.

shot.fallback: pirate captain raising a hidden blade

lines.text: And it works. Squard turns on the man who took him in like family.

shot.fallback: pirate captain striking an old emperor

lines.text: Notice the actual target of that whole scheme. It was never Whitebeard's body. It was Whitebeard's family.

shot.fallback: admiral watching a betrayal unfold

lines.text: A grudge decades old, reopened at exactly the right second, does more damage than another Admiral could.

shot.fallback: old strain reopening at the worst moment

lines.text: This isn't brute force winning the day. It's patience, and patience only makes sense in a longer game than one battle.

shot.fallback: admiral playing a slow, careful game

lines.text: Akainu runs the exact same play against Ace a few chapters later, except that time it costs a life.

shot.fallback: admiral repeating a familiar tactic

lines.text: Sengoku runs this whole deception as a coordinated operation, not one Admiral freelancing in the middle of a war.

shot.fallback: fleet admiral directing a wartime plan

lines.text: If you're wondering whether manipulation is really his style, chapter 573 removes any doubt...

shot.fallback: admiral smirking coldly

lines.text: By this point, Ace and Luffy are already running, already clear of the platform, almost out.

shot.fallback: two young pirates sprinting from danger

lines.text: Akainu catches up anyway, and instead of attacking first, he starts talking.

shot.fallback: admiral speaking calmly while pursuing

lines.text: He insults Whitebeard's age, his honor, his right to even call himself the strongest man alive.

shot.fallback: admiral mocking an absent emperor

lines.text: Ace stops running. Not because he's losing. Because nobody gets to say that about his captain.

shot.fallback: young pirate turning back furious

lines.text: He turns around and swings at Akainu, and the attack backfires immediately.

shot.fallback: fire fist striking a magma admiral

lines.text: Magma smothers fire. Akainu was always Ace's one real counter, Logia intangibility or not.

shot.fallback: molten rock overwhelming a flame

lines.text: Then Akainu does the part that decides this entire war: he aims past Ace, straight at Luffy.

shot.search: Akainu aims past Ace at Luffy
shot.fallback: admiral redirecting a fatal attack

lines.text: He says both brothers deserve the same fate for their parentage, and he means it as policy, not rage.

shot.fallback: admiral stating cold doctrine

lines.text: Ace throws himself in front of an attack that was never actually meant for him at all.

shot.fallback: young pirate shielding his brother

lines.text: Jinbe tries to block the follow-up aimed at finishing Ace off, and burns his own arm doing it.

shot.fallback: fish-man warrior shielding a fallen friend

lines.text: Marco and Vista throw themselves at Akainu right after, and he treats their Haki-coated strikes as a minor nuisance.

shot.fallback: two commanders striking an unmoved admiral

lines.text: None of that changes the outcome. Ace is gone minutes later, exactly the way the plan was built to end.

shot.fallback: fallen pirate at the center of a battlefield

lines.text: Every theory about this scene asks why Akainu went after Ace. Almost none ask why he was aiming at Luffy to begin with.

shot.fallback: admiral's fist aimed at a young pirate

lines.text: Because the lineage was always the mission. Ace just became the body that absorbed it...

shot.fallback: fallen pirate protecting his brother

lines.text: Here's where most retellings get the order backwards.

shot.fallback: battlefield narrative out of order

lines.text: Whitebeard doesn't go to war to fight Admirals. He goes to war to get Ace out alive.

shot.fallback: old emperor fighting for one purpose

lines.text: Right up until Ace falls, Whitebeard's violence stays reactive: block this, shield that, cover the retreat.

shot.fallback: emperor shielding his crew

lines.text: The moment Ace is gone, that changes instantly, and chapter 575 shows exactly how fast.

shot.fallback: emperor erupting with sudden fury

lines.text: Whitebeard turns on Akainu with real intent for the first time in this entire war, and nearly finishes him.

shot.fallback: emperor striking an admiral with fury

lines.text: Two point-blank quake punches split Marineford's island in half and barely slow the Admiral down.

shot.fallback: massive shockwave splitting a battlefield

lines.text: Even then, Akainu doesn't chase Whitebeard down afterward. He goes right back to chasing Luffy.

shot.fallback: admiral turning away toward a fleeing pirate

lines.text: Garp tries to end Akainu on the spot for what happened to Ace, and Sengoku has to physically hold him back.

shot.fallback: marine hero restrained by a fleet admiral

lines.text: That's Garp. A Marine hero for decades, turning on his own Fleet Admiral candidate in a single moment.

shot.fallback: veteran marine glaring at an admiral

lines.text: Akainu doesn't flinch from that either. In his doctrine, even a hero's grief doesn't outrank the mission.

shot.fallback: admiral unmoved by a grieving hero

lines.text: Whitebeard falls later that same arc, standing up, to Blackbeard's crew finishing what no Admiral managed.

shot.fallback: emperor standing tall against a crew

lines.text: Akainu never lands the finishing blow on Whitebeard. He was never actually assigned to.

shot.fallback: admiral walking away from an emperor

lines.text: Marco, Vista, Jinbe, and Crocodile combined only slow Akainu down enough for Luffy's escape, never for Whitebeard's safety.

shot.search: Marco Vista Jinbe Crocodile slow Akainu
shot.fallback: group of pirates straining against an admiral

lines.text: Crocodile, a former Warlord with zero loyalty to Whitebeard, still steps in once he sees exactly where that punch is really going.

shot.fallback: desert warlord blocking an admiral's strike

lines.text: Even an outsider reads the real target correctly faster than most of Whitebeard's own commanders do.

shot.fallback: former warlord recognizing the true threat

lines.text: It takes Shanks, a fourth Emperor, physically stepping between Akainu and Luffy to actually end that pursuit.

shot.fallback: red haired emperor halting an admiral

lines.text: Not Whitebeard's name. Not Whitebeard's crew. A separate Emperor is the only thing that works.

shot.fallback: lone emperor standing between two forces

lines.text: That single intervention matters more than anything three Admirals and a fleet of warships managed against Whitebeard's name all day.

shot.fallback: one emperor's arrival changing the battle

lines.text: After Whitebeard falls, Blackbeard takes his power, his territory, and his seat among the Four Emperors within the same arc.

shot.fallback: dark pirate standing over a fallen legacy

lines.text: Akainu barely reacts to any of it. He hears Blackbeard declare a new era and just keeps moving toward Luffy.

shot.fallback: admiral walking past a declaring pirate

lines.text: Even Doflamingo said, in chapter 801, that Whitebeard could have taken the title of Pirate King himself, if he'd ever actually wanted it.

shot.fallback: warlord recalling an old rival's choice

lines.text: He never wanted it. Which means he was never the lineage threat the World Government feared in the first place.

shot.fallback: old emperor uninterested in a crown

lines.text: Every fight Akainu picks across this entire war traces back to one of two names, and it's not the Emperor's...

shot.fallback: admiral's focus narrowing on two targets

lines.text: People will say I'm overselling this. Akainu still fights Whitebeard hard, burning a hole through his chest in chapter 568.

shot.fallback: admiral striking a strained emperor

lines.text: That's fair. Akainu never once backs down from a fight standing directly in front of him.

shot.fallback: admiral standing firm in battle

lines.text: But a man taking an opening in self-defense and a man hunting a lineage aren't running the same math.

shot.search: Akainu self defense versus lineage hunt
shot.fallback: admiral weighing two different fights

lines.text: Every time Akainu gets a clean choice between chasing Whitebeard or chasing Ace and Luffy, he picks the lineage.

shot.fallback: admiral choosing a target decisively

lines.text: He lets three of Whitebeard's own commanders slow him down and brushes them off, rather than ever turning back for the Emperor himself.

shot.fallback: admiral running past a declaring pirate

lines.text: He never once breaks off that chase to finish Whitebeard, even with the Emperor wide open.

shot.search: Akainu never breaks chase Whitebeard open
shot.fallback: admiral sprinting past a vulnerable emperor

lines.text: That's not an accident of combat. That's a target list, and Whitebeard was never actually on it.

shot.fallback: admiral's priorities laid bare

lines.text: My read: Akainu's Absolute Justice was never really about punishing pirates for what they do.

shot.fallback: admiral embodying a cold ideology

lines.text: It was about erasing what the World Government decided certain people simply are, from birth.

shot.fallback: shadowy government marking a lineage

lines.text: Whitebeard earned his fear the hard way, one fight at a time, across forty years at sea.

shot.fallback: legendary emperor built through decades

lines.text: Ace and Luffy never got the chance to earn theirs. Akainu decided it before either one threw a punch.

shot.fallback: two young pirates marked before battle

lines.text: Look at how the same math plays out years later on Egghead, when Sakazuki burns Kuma's face for simply existing near the World Nobles.

shot.fallback: admiral attacking a weakened figure

lines.text: Kuma isn't resisting. He's barely standing. Sakazuki still treats him as a problem that needs erasing on sight.

shot.fallback: weakened figure facing a merciless admiral

lines.text: That's the same hand that reached past Ace for Luffy, still running the identical program decades later.

shot.fallback: admiral unchanged across the years

lines.text: Even his own colleague Aokiji opposed Akainu's promotion for exactly this reason: his version of justice goes further than anyone needs it to.

shot.fallback: ice admiral arguing against a rival

lines.text: This isn't a hero keeping the peace. It's a system deciding who's allowed to exist before the fighting even starts.

shot.fallback: shadowy institution passing judgment

lines.text: Before Ace died, Yamato says Oden believed he was the one meant to finally stand against Kaido someday, which makes the loss hurt even more.

shot.fallback: giant warrior remembering an old prophecy

lines.text: Picture the counterfactual: if Whitebeard were the real target, three Admirals don't spend the first half of this war on crowd control.

shot.fallback: admirals managing chaos instead of a target

lines.text: On Elbaph right now, the Gorosei are hunting giants and lineages the exact same way, and I don't think that's a coincidence.

shot.fallback: five elders watching a giant island

lines.text: If this theory holds, expect the same math anytime another D. lineage surfaces in front of the Marines again.

shot.fallback: marine officers watching a new threat

lines.text: That's the version of Marineford I think the chapters actually drew, one target order at a time, long before the fire ever reached the platform.

shot.fallback: battlefield revealing its true shape

lines.text: Akainu chased Ace instead of Whitebeard because Whitebeard's strength dies with him. A lineage doesn't.

shot.fallback: admiral's true target finally clear

lines.text: And if you want to see what happens the day that lineage stops staying quiet, that's the next story.
